title: netwatch egress NDJSON export, netwatch.egress.v1.1
description: One line of the Egress tab's export. This validates a line, not a file. The first line is the header and every later line is a record. Later minors may add fields, so ignore any you do not know. A new record field bumps the minor in the schema name and adds a new schema file; a break needs netwatch 2.0. This file describes what netwatch 0.40 and later write; 0.39's header has no metadata block.

header.description: The first line of the file.

metadata.description: Names this output's schema. Every stable netwatch output has this block, at the same path.

netwatch_version.description: The netwatch that wrote this file.

record.description: One attributed destination of one process, with its policy verdict at export time. Metadata only, never payload.

sni.description: The destination's name, whatever the field is called: a TLS or QUIC SNI, or a cleartext HTTP Host. proto says tls only when a ClientHello supplied it. Absent, not null, when the flow carried no readable name.

asn_org.description: Organisation of the remote address, from the ASN database. Absent, not null, when no database resolved it.

ip.description: The most recent remote address. Can be empty in a baseline restored from a file that never held one.

proto.description: tls when a ClientHello named the destination, otherwise other, which includes a flow named by a cleartext HTTP Host. Before 0.40 such a flow said tls. Open set: a minor may split other into narrower values, so treat an unknown value as other.

ech.description: A flow to this destination used Encrypted ClientHello. Stays true once seen.

count.description: Connection-table ticks, about one a second, in which this destination appeared. A time spent connected, not a number of connections.

verdict.description: ok means a rule admitted it. drift means outside the process's allowlist. blocked means it matched a block entry. undeclared means no rule under a policy that declares itself complete. unchecked means nothing was compared, because the process has no rule or no policy is loaded. unreadable means Encrypted ClientHello hid the name. Open set: a minor may add a verdict, so treat an unknown value as not ok.

matched_by.description: What admitted an ok verdict: sni for a declared hostname, ip for a declared address, and asn for a whole autonomous system. sni also covers a rule that declares no name restriction at all, so it does not always mean one named endpoint. Null for every other verdict. Open set: a minor may add a way of matching, including a broader value for such a rule, so treat an unknown value as broad.

bytes_out.description: Approximate, from per-tick rates. Zero when no capture ran, which does not mean no traffic.

bytes_in.description: Approximate, from per-tick rates. Zero when no capture ran, which does not mean no traffic.
